decision_clues.physical_effect: High absorption in visible/NIR via interference and multiple reflections; high IR reflection from bottom Al.
conditions_and_unknowns: Specific thicknesses (90/10/80 nm) are for a specific design point; optimal values for strict 400-700 vs 700-2000 split may differ.

decision_clues.inference_bridge: Hypothesize that replacing SiO2 with HfO2 (higher index) or adjusting the dielectric thickness ratio can sharpen the transition between the absorption band (visible) and reflection band (NIR) to better match the task's specific cutoff at 700 nm.

routes.claim: A simple D/M/D/M stack (Dielectric/Metal/Dielectric/Metal) using HfO2/SiO2 mix and Cr/Al can achieve the spectral split via a single Fabry-Perot cavity tuned to the visible.
transfer_assumptions: The SiO2/Cr/Al mechanism transfers to HfO2/SiO2/Cr/Al by adjusting thickness for the higher index of HfO2.
A single absorbing Cr layer is sufficient if the cavity Q-factor is optimized.

expectations.controlled_conditions: Same material order, substrate, incident medium, 0-degree unpolarized illumination.
expectations.reason: Optimizing the cavity resonance to center on the visible band should reduce average reflectance (increase absorption) in G1.

expectations.controlled_conditions: Same material order, substrate, incident medium, 0-degree unpolarized illumination.
expectations.reason: Shifting the absorption peak strictly into the visible should restore high reflectance in the NIR band.

routes.model_knowledge_rationale: While evidence supports the D/M/D/M topology, the specific substitution of HfO2 as the first layer to tune the input impedance for air incidence relies on standard thin-film physics (higher index reduces physical thickness for quarter-wave condition) rather than a specific cited value for this exact stack.

routes.claim: Using HfO2 as the sole dielectric spacer maximizes the refractive index contrast, allowing thinner layers to achieve the same phase shift, potentially reducing parasitic absorption in thicker dielectrics.
transfer_assumptions: High-index HfO2 can replace low-index SiO2 entirely if thicknesses are scaled down.
Thinner layers reduce the probability of defects and stress.

expectations.controlled_conditions: Same number of layers; dielectric material changed to pure HfO2.
expectations.reason: Higher index contrast may provide better impedance matching at the air interface with thinner layers.

routes.model_knowledge_rationale: Evidence cites HfO2 for thermal stability; the optical advantage of an all-HfO2 spacer system for visible/NIR splitting is a physical inference based on index contrast principles, not explicitly claimed in the source for this spectral range.

routes.claim: Optimizing the thickness of the bottom Cr layer specifically for IR reflectance while keeping the top structure optimized for visible absorption.
transfer_assumptions: The bottom metal layer thickness primarily influences IR reflectance once it exceeds the skin depth.
Visible absorption is dominated by the top cavity.

expectations.controlled_conditions: Top cavity fixed; only bottom Cr thickness varied.
expectations.reason: Increasing the bottom Cr thickness ensures it acts as an opaque mirror for NIR, minimizing transmission into the substrate (if any) and maximizing reflection.

routes.model_knowledge_rationale: Evidence supports the role of the bottom metal as an IR reflector. The specific decoupling assumption that thickening it beyond ~20nm yields diminishing returns for visible absorption but helps NIR reflectance is based on skin-depth physics.
